passages.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The modern obsession with productivity has bequeathed us a curious (1)______: the more contrivances we invent to economise time, the less of it we appear to possess. A century ago the labour-saving device was hailed as an emancipator, a benevolent servant that would hand the common man the leisure once monopolised by the aristocracy. Today the same device functions as an exacting taskmaster. Had our forebears foreseen this inversion, they (2)______ their faith in machinery with rather more circumspection. The smartphone, that most (3)______ of companions, promises liberation while quietly colonising every interstice of the day — the queue, the commute, the dinner table, the sleepless hour before dawn. Sociologists have christened this condition ‘time famine’, a scarcity that is psychological rather than arithmetical, for the hours have not contracted; only our capacity to inhabit them has withered. The malady is aggravated by a culture that treats busyness as a badge of moral worth, so that the executive who boasts of sleeping four hours a night is admired rather than pitied. (4)______ we persist in regarding efficiency as an unqualified good, we shall continue to mistake velocity for direction and motion for progress. The remedy proposed by a growing body of thinkers is neither Luddite nor (5)______; nobody seriously proposes smashing the looms or retreating to a hermitage in the hills. It is, rather, the deliberate cultivation of idleness — unstructured, unmonetised, gloriously purposeless time in which the mind is permitted to wander without the obligation to produce. Such reverie, the neuroscientists assure us, is not indolence but incubation: the default network of the brain stitching together the scattered fragments of experience into insight. Perhaps the most radical act available to the contemporary citizen is simply to sit still and do nothing at all.
